Find the animals a pedigree can lose because they are unavailable

Source: R/findUnavailable.R
findUnavailable.Rd

The ids shrinkPedigree removes in its first trim, in the order it removes them: animals that are not genotyped and have no genotyped descendant (ungenotyped leaves, removed until none is left); then each founder couple with one child together and no other mate when neither founder is genotyped (the child becomes a founder); then each founder left with no offspring (a stray marry-in), genotyped or not.

Usage

findUnavailable(ped, genotyped)

Arguments

ped

a pedigree data.frame with the fields id, sire and dam.

genotyped

a logical vector, one value per row of ped, TRUE where the animal is genotyped (or otherwise available). NA is not allowed.

Value

A character vector of ids in the order they are removed; character(0) when none is.

Details

It is the step of shrinkPedigree() that kinship2's findUnavailable() performs, from a pedigree data frame instead of a kinship2 pedigree object. Two differences: when no animal is genotyped, kinship2's function stops with an error, and this one returns every id; and when removing an ungenotyped founder couple makes its ungenotyped child a founder, this function, like shrinkPedigree(), removes in the same trim the couple that child forms with another ungenotyped founder, if that couple's child comes later in ped, where kinship2 leaves that couple for its next step. On every pedigree its tests compare, this function and findAvailNonInform together remove the same animals as kinship2::pedigree.shrink()'s first two steps. An animal may have one known parent.

It stops with shrinkPedigree()'s message for a bad pedigree or a genotyped vector of the wrong length or with an NA.

References

Sinnwell JP, Therneau TM, Schaid DJ (2014). "The kinship2 R Package for Pedigree Data." Human Heredity, 78(2), 91-93.

See also

shrinkPedigree, findAvailNonInform, findAvailAffected, bitSize

Examples

## D, G and I are ungenotyped leaves; then A and B are an ungenotyped
## founder couple with one child, C; then H is a founder with no offspring
ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "I"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", NA, "C", "C", NA, "H"),
  dam = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", NA, "E", "E", NA, "E"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
genotyped <- c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
findUnavailable(ped, genotyped)
#> [1] "D" "G" "I" "A" "B" "H"
